identity.name: MANORAMA INDUSTRIES LTD
identity.industry: Specialty Fats & Cocoa Butter Equivalents (CBE) / Edible Oil Value Chain

summary.oneLiner: Manorama Industries delivered exceptional FY26 with 76% revenue growth and 27% EBITDA margins driven by volume surge and high-value CBE mix (now 30% of sales), while initiating a INR 460 Cr capex cycle for African backward integration and forward capacity expansion to sustain >25% growth trajectory through FY28.

one-line thesis: Manorama Industries delivered exceptional FY26 with 76% revenue growth and 27% EBITDA margins driven by volume surge and high-value CBE mix (now 30% of sales), while initiating a INR 460 Cr capex cycle for African backward integration and forward capacity expansion to sustain >25% growth trajectory through FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,358 Cr (+76% YoY); EBITDA: INR 368 Cr (27.1% margin, +40bps YoY); PAT: INR 233 Cr (17.2% margin, normalized for INR 23.3 Cr cumulative FX MTM loss); Order Book: Not disclosed (demand-led production); Net Debt: INR ~200 Cr (Debt/Equity 0.38x), One-offs: INR 23.3 Cr FX MTM provision, INR ~13.5 Cr subsidiary startup losses.
guidance: Revenue Growth: >25% (FY27); Margin: Sustain 25%-27% EBITDA; Order Inflow: Strong visibility from global F&B/Cosmetic demand; Capex: INR 460 Cr over 2-3 years (commissioning by FY28).
order book & pipeline: Demand-led model with 85%-90% utilization target on expanded 52k TPA capacity; no formal order book disclosed but visibility high via long-term customer partnerships.
segment / subsidiary detail: CBE contributed ~30% of revenue (up from 10% two years ago); Stearin + CBE constitute 70%-75% of value-added mix; Solvent Fractionation Plant 2 debottlenecked to 32.5k TPA (+30%), Plant 1 (15k TPA) to follow; Total input capacity heading to 52k TPA.
growth verticals / optionality: Burkina Faso plant (INR 120 Cr) for seed-to-butter conversion (45%-60% RM cost savings, yield improvement); New 75k TPA Solvent Fractionation Plant 3 + CBE facility + 200 TPD refinery (INR 330-340 Cr) for forward integration; Targeting INR 3,500 Cr revenue by FY30.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin pressure in consolidated entities (43% vs 48% prior) due to subsidiary startup costs/freight; Standalone margins stable at ~48%; Expect normalization as subsidiaries scale; Logistic cost savings from Africa integration to offset freight inflation.
capex / expansion: INR 460 Cr total (INR 52 Cr spent in FY26); INR 120 Cr for Burkina Faso backward integration; INR 330-340 Cr for forward integration (CBE, Fractionation, Refinery); Phased commissioning by FY28; Funded via internal accruals (INR 260 Cr operating cash flow) and existing cash (INR 130 Cr FD); QIP (INR 500 Cr) is enabling only, not immediate.
capital allocation: Prioritizing high-ROCE capex (>6x asset turn expected on forward projects); Working capital cycle improved to 125 days (from 151); ROCE 33.6%, ROE 40.3%; No dividend change discussed, focus on reinvestment.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension (West Africa, West Asia) impacting freight/energy; FX volatility (60% hedged, 40% open); Subsidiary ramp-up delays; Raw material price fluctuation (Shea, Sal, Mango).
management quality / tone: Highly confident, execution-focused, emphasizing long-term vision over quarterly noise; transparent on subsidiary losses as transitional; aggressive on capacity utilization and margin sustainability.
non-obvious takeaways: Annual cash profit (PAT+Dep) of INR 259 Cr now exceeds gross block (INR 250 Cr), signaling extreme capital efficiency; Burkina Faso project is government-backed (MoU signed) mitigating political risk; Immediate seed processing in Africa improves fat yield vs. 60-day transport lag.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs and supply chain inefficiencies in traditional edible oil processors | Manorama Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Backward integration in Africa directly addresses 45%-60% of RM cost while improving yield; high-value CBE mix (30% of sales) provides pricing power and margin resilience against commodity cycles. |

themes.title: Agri value-chain - food processing, dairy, protein & seeds
themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Niche, high-return specialty fats platform with a ~2-decade track record, built on an end-to-end integrated model from exotic tree-borne seed sourcing (India, Africa) through to global CBE/specialty-fats leadership ("Forest to Formulation").
- Long-standing relationships with Fortune 500 food & confectionery majors (Ferrero, Mondelez, Mars, Hershey, Nestle, Barry Callebaut, Cargill, AAK, Fuji Oil, among others) and personal-care brands (The Body Shop, L'Oreal Paris, Lush), supported by customized product development.
- Geographic reach spans 39+ countries across Asia, Europe, Americas, MENA, Africa and Oceania via 10 international subsidiaries; Export:Domestic revenue mix stood at 60:40 in Q1FY27.
- Government of India Recognized Star Export House with MSME ZED GOLD certification, alongside international certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, RSPO, Kosher, Halal/MUI, FSSC 22000, EcoVadis, Sedex SMETA) enabling access to premium global markets.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Awards] Multiple export-excellence recognitions cited in the deck, including the IOPEPC Award for Highest Excellence in Exports of Shea Oil (2024-25), GLOBOIL INDIA 2025 Award for highest exports of Made-in-India CBE, SHEFEXIL Export Excellence Award for 7 consecutive years, and FIEO's 'Highest Foreign Exchange Earner' awards.
- [Leadership] Board led by Ashish Saraf (Chairman & Managing Director) and Vinita Saraf (Vice Chairperson & Whole Time Director), with CA Ashok Jain as Whole Time Director & CFO; R&D led by Dr. Krishnadath Bhaggan (Deputy CEO – Business Development & VP R&D) at a DSIR-certified, Government of India-accredited research center.
- [Shareholding] As of June 2026, Promoter holding was 54.32%, FIIs 3.22%, MF 2.63% and Other 39.83%; Market Cap was INR 10,270 Cr and CMP ₹1,626 (as on 12 Aug 2026).
